Findings come mainly from the **AXEL Chat Efficiency Audit Report** in parent transcript [`ef94eb64-2da7-4be5-b1ef-a1704d663ee0`](ef94eb64-2da7-4be5-b1ef-a1704d663ee0). That chat implemented **HIGH** (and a follow-on chat addressed **MEDIUM** M1–M3 per [`fc72fabf-b615-4e6b-ba56-ce6990907fed`](fc72fabf-b615-4e6b-ba56-ce6990907fed)), but the audit’s **LOW / optional hygiene** items were left as future work.

### Deferred LOW-priority workflow items (parent transcript sourced)

- **[Chat efficiency audit](ef94eb64-2da7-4be5-b1ef-a1704d663ee0)** — **L1:** Archive or remove very large inactive debug logs under `logs/debug/` (hundreds of MB each) so they do not clutter disk or get opened accidentally (`debug-1d1bdd.log`, `debug-c9d495.log` were called out).
- **[Chat efficiency audit](ef94eb64-2da7-4be5-b1ef-a1704d663ee0)** — **L2:** **QA run log archival** — move bulk JSON history to something like `qa/archive/*.json`, keep only the last few entries in the main `AXEL_QA_RUN_LOG.md`, and extend `update_qa_analytics.py` so analytics can still see archived runs if needed.
- **[Chat efficiency audit](ef94eb64-2da7-4be5-b1ef-a1704d663ee0)** — **L3:** **Split “plan” and “implement” chats** — after planning, start a fresh implementation chat with a short pointer to the plan instead of carrying the full planning transcript through many edit turns.

### Note on coverage

Other recent parent transcripts did not surface additional **explicit LOW / later** workflow bullets comparable to that ranked “LOW priority (optional hygiene)” table; most other hits were gameplay/items (e.g. `L1`/`L2` item IDs) or subagent-only notes, which you asked to exclude from the parent set.
